citations.assessment: Rav Acha bar Adda attaches the teaching of five distinctions to the end of the mishnah.
The text gives both a direct Acha bar Adda statement and a version through Hamnuna and Rav.
Acha son of Rava asks about the ladder. The passage then quotes Acha bar Adda through Hamnuna in Rav’s name in the reply to that question.
The first chain has Acha bar Adda in Rav’s name, and the other has Acha bar Abba transmitting through Hamnuna from Rav.
Explicitly identifies this Rav Pappa as Acha bar Adda’s son. Eruvin supplies the same full patronym.
Rav Pappa says he heard from his father, whose source was Rav. No identification with another Rav Pappa is made.
On arriving Acha bar Adda reports dividing the verse into three in the West.
The parallel also names Rav Acha bar Adda and the western division of the verse.
Reports Rav Yehudah’s statement on giving terumah.
Reports Rabbi Yitzchak about the series of decrees.
The parallel also names the Rabbi Yitzchak chain.
The attribution to Ulla is explicit.
Rava allowed Rabbi Acha bar Adda to sleep outside the sukkah. The neighboring notice is about Acha Bardela.
The forger explains the tremulous signature; Rashbam reads the support as a rope. The Bavli identifies the tremor, with age supplied in Heilprin and in the local interpretive tradition.
Acha son of Rav Adda directly asks Rav Ashi about Rami bar Chama’s inference. This text leaves Ashi’s generation unqualified.
The text reports the birth and death succession that Heilprin uses in his chronological argument. It does not determine which Ashi appears in Bava Metzia.
The internal dossier provides the proposed earlier figure and preserves the source’s argument rather than adjudicating it as chronology.
This entry bears the complete final name. The bare mention in 302 does not specify a relationship.
